## Q-scope-01 · Which products and pages should this system cover, and which should it leave out?
Zoom 0 sketch · weight high · changes 8 decisions · class I · cards DC-L11-02
- **Ask:** "Is this only for your app, or also your marketing site, docs, emails or in-house tools?"
- **Why:** What the system covers sets how general your components must be. It also sets how many layers of design tokens you need [DC-L11-02].
- **Options:**
  - `product-app` Product app: tight, opinionated visuals are possible when this is the only surface [DC-L11-02, inferred].
    - Now: Parts are built for your app alone, so the look can stay tight and specific. [inferred] As it grows: Adding a marketing site or emails later means making parts more general and adding token layers.
  - `marketing` Marketing site: adds an expressive layer next to the productive one (Carbon splits productive and expressive type and motion) [DC-L06-01].
    - Now: Adds a louder, expressive layer for the marketing site next to the calm app layer, as Carbon does. As it grows: Marketing and app styles tend to drift apart, so someone must keep the shared colors and type in step.
  - `internal-tools` Internal or admin tools: usually dense (see Q-aud-01) [inferred].
    - Now: In-house tools are usually dense: smaller text and tighter rows so more fits on screen. [inferred] As it grows: Each new tool reuses the same parts; dense screens get a compact mode instead of a second system.
  - `docs-content` Docs or content site: long-form reading pushes line length and paragraph rules (DC-L02-17) [inferred].
    - Now: Long reading pages add rules for comfortable line length and paragraph spacing. [inferred] As it grows: If articles pass about a third of your pages, a second, bigger set of heading styles pays off.
  - `email` Email: a constrained rendering target the token pipeline must also output [DC-L11-02 options].
    - Now: Email can show only simple styling, so the system must also write its colors and text out for email. As it grows: Every new email template reuses those outputs; anything email cannot show needs a plain fallback. [inferred]
  - `partner-embed` Inside partner sites or apps: need scoped, context-agnostic components ("card", not "product card").
    - Now: Parts must work inside other people's sites, so they get general names like 'card', not 'product card'. As it grows: Partners build on your parts, so changes need public docs and stricter version numbers.
- **Default:** `product-app`: product-app only *Source:* card heuristic, scope v1 to what the pilot touches [DC-L11-02].
- **Show:** a strip with one sample screen per selected surface, all rendered from the same draft tokens.
- **Skip:** yes, defaults to a single product app.

## Q-scope-06 · What kind of screens does this system mostly serve?
Zoom 0 sketch · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Ask:** "What are these screens mostly for: selling, getting work done, reading, or enjoying an experience?"
- **Why:** A sales page, a work tool, a help page and a showcase need different spacing, card use and big "hero" moments. Naming the kind of screen sets those rules.
- **Options:**
  - `operate` Operate (app screens where people get work done): spacing follows Q-aud-01, no hero, cards only to group related data; 14px body text at middle density [DC-L02-08].
  - `persuade` Persuade (marketing and landing pages): roomy spacing, one big hero line, sections rather than card grids; display sizes reach further [DC-L02-11].
  - `read` Read (docs, articles and help): comfortable spacing, 16px body text, no cards around running text [DC-L02-08].
  - `experience` Experience (portfolios, showcases and games): roomy spacing, big imagery and hero moments; display sizes reach further [DC-L02-11].
- **Default:** `operate`: operate *Source:* the engine's default product type (work-tool) is an Operate surface [inferred].
- **Show:** the same sample content as each chosen surface, side by side.
- **Dials:** none. Expression and Density stay one setting for the whole system. The main surface sets `raw.productType` (Operate work-tool, Read content, Persuade and Experience marketing), which moves body size; any Persuade or Experience surface sets `raw.marketingSurfaces`, which widens the display sizes. Each surface also gets its own density mode and hero rule in DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md [inferred].
- **Use / avoid:** use one mode per surface; avoid treating a whole product as Persuade because it has one landing page.
- **Skip:** yes, defaults to operate.

## Q-scope-07 · What phase is the project in: an idea, being built, close to launch, or live?
Zoom 0 sketch · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Ask:** "Where is the project now: an idea, being built, close to launch, or live with real users?"
- **Why:** The project's phase changes which questions come first. An idea needs its purpose and an analogous product before any screen; a product close to launch needs an audit of what exists, its copy and a preflight; a live product needs the audit and rules for who may change the system [DC-L11-04, DC-L19-179, DC-L11-21; inferred from the owner's direction of 2026-11-02, OWNER-FEEDBACK row 6].
- **Options:**
  - `idea` An idea, no code yet: the alignment first (mission, vision, purpose, goals) and the analogous product, then the sketch; there is nothing to audit yet [inferred].
  - `building` Being built: the sketch, then the areas the screens being built need most [inferred].
  - `near-launch` Close to launch: an audit of the screens that exist (the interface inventory), then copy and voice, then preflight before release; launch and share surfaces join the scope [DC-L11-04, DC-L19-179].
  - `live` Live, with real users: the audit first, mapping onto the tokens the code already has, then governance and versioning [DC-L19-189, DC-L11-21].
- **Default:** none: read from the repo first (no code: idea; code without deploy settings: building; code with deploy settings: near launch; a changelog with released versions, or a version past 1.0.0: live). An empty folder says nothing, so ask once *Source:* the owner's direction of 2026-11-02 (OWNER-FEEDBACK row 6) and its proposal [inferred].
- **Show:** none visual; the next-step offer after the sketch leads with what this phase needs first (zoom.md, "The project's phase").
- **Use / avoid:** use the phase to choose what to offer first; avoid asking a near-launch product the idea-phase questions again, and avoid reading npm's default version 1.0.0 as a release [inferred].
- **Skip:** yes; when nothing shows the phase, the offer after the sketch stays as it is.

## Q-scope-02 · Is there existing UI to clean up and merge, or is this a new product?
Zoom 2 defined · weight medium · changes 2 decisions · class I · cards DC-L11-04
- **Ask:** "Do you have screens already that we should clean up and merge, or are we starting fresh?"
- **Why:** Checking the screens you have (an audit) shows how much to merge. For example, 40 grays can merge into one 10-step color ramp [DC-L11-04, inferred].
- **Options:**
  - `greenfield` New product: skip the audit and go straight to visual language.
  - `manual-inventory` Existing screens, sorted by hand: screenshots across 16 categories, then keep/merge/kill decisions (Brad Frost).
  - `automated-audit` Existing screens, counted by a tool: unique colors and declarations (CSS Stats), component and prop usage (Omlet, react-scanner), Figma library analytics.
  - `both` Both: automated counts plus the manual inventory for shared vocabulary [DC-L11-04 default].
- **Default:** `greenfield`: greenfield; if existing UI, `both` *Source:* card heuristic, the manual inventory's main value is shared vocabulary and buy-in [DC-L11-04].
- **Show:** an inventory board: counts of unique colors, type styles and button variants found, with the proposed consolidated ramp beside them.
- **Skip:** yes, defaults to greenfield.

## Q-scope-05 · What are you starting from: a product you have, a UI kit, a site you like, or only a brief?
Zoom 2 defined · weight medium · changes 2 decisions · class I · cards DC-L17-02, DC-L11-01, DC-L17-03
- **Ask:** "Where do we start: your product, a UI kit, a site you admire, or a blank page and a brief?"
- **Why:** A kit makes your system look like the kit, and a reference passes on its rhythm. A brief gives the widest range of looks but needs the most choices. Using a system as is, adapting one or making your own sets the cost [DC-L17-02, DC-L11-01].
- **Options:**
  - `existing-product` From an existing product: audit and extract, then consolidate (the interface inventory; see Q-scope-02) [DC-L17-02; DC-L11-04].
  - `ui-kit` From a UI kit or library (Untitled UI, Material 3 kit, shadcn): fast, but the kit's defaults become the look unless changed (the M3 kit shipped 6 versions in 12 months) [DC-L17-02].
  - `reference` From a reference you admire: carry structure and quality, never identity (gstack and Stitch support this) [DC-L17-02].
  - `brief` From a brief only: interview, then generate directions [DC-L17-02].
  - `adopt|adapt|create` Use as is, adapt, or build your own: adopt a system as-is (Material, Carbon, Fluent), adapt a themeable base (shadcn create, Radix Themes), or create your own; NN/g ranks their cost lowest to highest [DC-L11-01].
  - `reinterpret|replicate-swap|flag-only` How close to stay to the reference: reinterpret the lessons (default), replicate structure with every identity element swapped (only for "our version of this"), or read a competitor only to list shared tropes; copying identity is never offered [DC-L17-03].
- **Default:** existing product: audit first; otherwise brief first with an optional reference, a kit only as a component base (Q-comp-01), not as the visual direction; small teams adapt an accessible base; references reinterpreted *Source:* card heuristics [DC-L17-02, DC-L11-01, DC-L17-03].
- **Show:** the three starting points side by side on one screen, with "carried from reference" and "swapped" labels on each element.
- **Use / avoid:** use a kit for components and a reference for structure; avoid letting either become the brand ("websites made with shadcn/ui famously look the same") [DC-L11-01].
- **Skip:** yes, brief first.

## Q-site-01 · What must the site achieve, and how will you know it worked?
Zoom 1 broad · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Show if:** a site that persuades: Q-scope-06 includes `persuade`, or Q-scope-01 includes `marketing`
- **Ask:** "What should the site get done, and how will you count it? For example: booked demos from senior buyers, about ten a month."
- **Why:** The goal decides what every page leads with and which action gets the main button. Sections are chosen for the goal they serve [DC-L15-03].
- **Options:**
  - `demos` Booked demos or sales calls: one main button to book, repeated after each proof section [inferred].
  - `signups` Sign-ups or trials: the button starts the product, and a real screen of it sits near the top [inferred].
  - `purchases` Purchases: the price and what is included come before the button [inferred].
  - `enquiries` Enquiries or quotes: a short form, and who answers it and how soon [inferred].
  - `installs` App installs: store badges, and the app's own screens instead of a mock-up [inferred].
  - `understanding` Understanding and trust, with no direct action: explainers lead and the button is secondary [inferred].
- **Default:** none: drafted from the one action recorded at the sketch; the measure is theirs to give *Source:* owner inputs are never invented [DC-L17-08].
- **Show:** none visual; PRODUCT.md's Site brief shows the goal and its measure.
- **Use / avoid:** use one goal per site, with a measure; avoid two equal main actions on one page [DC-L15-03].
- **Skip:** yes; PRODUCT.md then says Not enough information (Q-site-01).

## Q-site-02 · Which roles must the site convince, and what does each need to see?
Zoom 1 broad · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Show if:** a site that persuades: Q-scope-06 includes `persuade`, or Q-scope-01 includes `marketing`
- **Ask:** "Who has to say yes, and what does each of them need to see? For example: the operations head needs the outcome, IT needs security, finance needs the price."
- **Why:** A business purchase is often decided by several people with different questions: the person who will use it, the one who signs, the one who checks security or cost. One page for everyone answers none of them well [inferred].
- **Options:**
  - `user` The person who will use it every day: a real screen, and how their day gets easier [inferred].
  - `buyer` The person who signs: the outcome in numbers, and named clients like them [inferred].
  - `technical` The person who checks it fits (IT, security, engineering): integrations, security and data handling, on a page of their own [inferred].
  - `finance` The person who checks the cost: the price, or how pricing works [inferred].
  - `single` One kind of visitor who decides alone (a shop, a club, an app): one path and no role pages [inferred].
- **Default:** none: drafted from the user research or their words *Source:* owner inputs are never invented [DC-L17-08].
- **Show:** none visual; PRODUCT.md's Site brief lists each role and what it needs to see.
- **Use / avoid:** use a role's need to choose its section or page; avoid one generic "for teams" message aimed at every role [inferred].
- **Skip:** yes; PRODUCT.md then says Not enough information (Q-site-02).

## Q-site-03 · What can you prove, and may we show it?
Zoom 1 broad · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Show if:** a site that persuades: Q-scope-06 includes `persuade`, or Q-scope-01 includes `marketing`
- **Ask:** "What can you prove? Clients you may name, quotes with a name and role, and figures with what they mean: for whom, over what time, compared with what."
- **Why:** Proof carries a page that persuades: named clients, quotes, outcome figures. Invented proof is a deceptive pattern (fake social proof), and a figure without its qualifier overclaims [DC-L13-15].
- **Options:**
  - `clients` Named clients, with their permission: a line of names or logos [inferred].
  - `testimonials` Quotes with a real name and role.
  - `figures` Outcome figures with their qualifier: the number, for whom, over what time, compared with what [inferred].
  - `credentials` Certifications, awards or standards met, with where to check them [inferred].
  - `none-yet` Nothing to show yet: pages lead with how it works and a real product screen, with no placeholder logos or quotes [DC-L13-15].
- **Default:** none: only the person has it. The proof in a confirmed positioning (research.md section 8) fills the line until they answer *Source:* fake social proof is a deceptive pattern [DC-L13-15].
- **Show:** none visual; PRODUCT.md's Site brief lists each proof, and flags a figure with no qualifier.
- **Use / avoid:** use only what they gave, in their words; avoid placeholder logos, "trusted by" with no names, and rounded-up figures [DC-L13-15].
- **Skip:** yes; PRODUCT.md then says Not enough information (Q-site-03), and pages leave proof sections out.

## Q-site-04 · How should people find the site, and in which languages?
Zoom 1 broad · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Show if:** a site that persuades: Q-scope-06 includes `persuade`, or Q-scope-01 includes `marketing`
- **Ask:** "How do people find you: search, AI answers such as ChatGPT or Perplexity, links you send, or social posts? In which languages? And which questions should the site answer?"
- **Why:** How people arrive shapes the pages: search needs a page for each question people ask, AI answer tools need those answers in the page's text, and each language needs its own pages [inferred].
- **Options:**
  - `search` Search engines: a page for each main question, each with its own title, description and one main heading [inferred].
  - `answer` Answer boxes and voice answers: each question answered in the first sentence under its heading [inferred].
  - `generative` AI answer tools (generative engines): ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI answers read the page's text, so answers, names and figures sit in plain text, not only inside images or scripts [inferred]. In one study with a 2023 engine, real quotations, statistics and cited sources raised a page's share of the answer by 27 to 41% and keyword stuffing lowered it; the quotes and figures must be the owner's own proof from Q-site-03, with its qualifiers.
  - `links` Links you send (sales emails, decks, events): each link lands on a page that keeps the link's promise [inferred].
  - `social` Social posts: each page has its own share image and title [inferred].
- **Default:** none: languages read from the repo, else the language they write in; channels and questions are theirs *Source:* [inferred].
- **Show:** none visual; PRODUCT.md's Site brief lists the channels, languages and questions.
- **Use / avoid:** use the questions buyers really ask (from the research or sales calls); avoid keyword lists with no page that answers them [inferred].
- **Skip:** yes; PRODUCT.md then says Not enough information (Q-site-04).

## Q-site-05 · Which kinds of pages does the site need?
Zoom 1 broad · weight medium · changes 0 decisions · class I
- **Show if:** a site that persuades: Q-scope-06 includes `persuade`, or Q-scope-01 includes `marketing`
- **Ask:** "Which kinds of pages does the site need? I read these from your repo; add or remove any."
- **Why:** Page families are the site's structure. Each family shares one layout and one job, so pages stay consistent and the structure is not invented page by page [inferred].
- **Options:**
  - `platform` Platform or product: what it does, a page per main feature [inferred].
  - `industry` Industry or use case: a page per kind of customer, each with its own proof [inferred].
  - `explainer` Explainers: how it works, guides, and the questions from Q-site-04 [inferred].
  - `company` Company and proof: about, team, customers, case studies, contact.
  - `pricing` Pricing: the price, or how pricing works [inferred].
  - `legal` Legal and trust: privacy, terms, cookies, security [inferred].
- **Default:** none: read from the repo's routes; an idea gets the families its goal and roles need *Source:* [inferred].
- **Show:** none visual; PRODUCT.md's Site brief lists the families, and the structure step draws one wireframe per family.
- **Use / avoid:** use one layout per family; avoid a page that belongs to no family [inferred].
- **Skip:** yes; PRODUCT.md then says Not enough information (Q-site-05).
